newsitem.title: UK: Pakistan's three-year dollar Eurobond due May -ANZ.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's three-year dollar Eurobond due May -ANZ.

text.p: Pakistan is expected to launch a three-year dollar Eurobond next month following roadshows which kick off on May 5, a syndicate official at lead manager ANZ Investment Bank said.
He said the amount would be for a minimum of $100 million. Price talk was roughly 350 to 400 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, he said.
The tentative roadshow plans are to visit Tokyo, Seoul, Singapore, London, two cities in the Middle East and New York.
ANZ -- the largest foreign bank operating in Pakistan -- was mandated to lead manage the bond in February.
At the time ANZ said the bond would represent the first opportunity for investors to gain exposure to Pakistan following the election in February.

In December 1994 Pakistan launched a $150 million 11.50 percent December 1999 bond. It was launched to yield 385 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes, was trading at around 415 b.p. over in February and had tightened to 374 b.p. over on Wednesday, dealers said.
Pakistan is rated B2 by Moody's Investors Service and B+ by Standard & Poor's Corp.
